Cross-Benchmark Transfer from RL on Agentic Coding Tasks

paper.arxiv.2610.00890

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2610.00890v1. Protected regression tests/no-oracle task construction and shared TerminalBench family protocol establish training/evaluation scope. Six evaluated benchmarks do not become six independent families or causal transfer proof. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Headline DeepSWE and Terminal-Bench 2.1 baselines are public scores, whereas other baselines are in-house; DeepSWE’s in-house base differs from its public baseline. Terminal-Bench 4 revises 3 and is not an independent task family, and eight trained Terminal 3 runs were excluded for harness failures. These provenance/denominator distinctions must accompany cross-benchmark aggregation.

Permanent record ID: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2610.00890.limitation

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Experts author 1,000 repository-change tasks and 700 terminal tasks. RL is used without a supervised stage; regression tests gate repository reward, while terminal tasks have no pass-to-pass gate.
  • Partial credit is over equally weighted checks/verifier criteria, not necessarily one vote per semantic requirement; a requirement can map to one or more checks.
  • Headline DeepSWE and Terminal-Bench 2.1 baselines are public scores. The in-house DeepSWE baseline differs; Terminal-Bench 2.1 has no in-house base run, and its public baseline averages three runs.
  • Terminal-Bench 4 revises Terminal-Bench 3 and forms one family for pooled analysis. Eight trained Terminal-Bench 3 runs were excluded for harness failures, leaving eight passes among 66 scored runs.
  • The report uses one final trained checkpoint/run. Paired behavioral examples focus on newly solved tasks and do not isolate causal effects of each task or reward property.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The experiment applies one GSPO epoch with a rank 32 LoRA adapter to Kimi K2.7 Code on 1000 expert-built repository tasks and 700 terminal tasks, without a supervised stage. Reward is target-check fraction, but any failed pass-to-pass regression test zeroes repository reward; terminal tasks have no such regression-test gate.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

For SWE-BenchPro’s 731-task public split under mini-swe-agent, Table 2 reports pass@1 increasing 60.1→64.8%, or 35 additional solved tasks, in matched in-house base/trained runs. This is one trained checkpoint/run and does not establish generalization uncertainty over training seeds.
